      "author": "Zorba-the-buddhah",
      "number": 17551,
      "repository": "elizaos/eliza",
      "body": "## Problem\n\nOn a fork PR from a first-time contributor, GitHub holds every\n`pull_request`-triggered workflow at `action_required` until a maintainer\napproves the run. Both aggregate gates trigger on `pull_request_target`, which is\nexempt from that approval, so they start immediately and poll for checks that\ncannot appear. After the full timeout budget they convert \"never appeared\" into\n`FAILED`.\n\nThe result is a PR whose required checks are all red without any of them having\nevaluated the diff, and roughly 20-40 minutes of runner time consumed per gate,\nper PR, producing no signal.\n\n## Evidence\n\nTwo PRs, different sizes, different subsystems, same failure:\n\n| PR | Diff | Develop PR Gate | Security Advisory Gate |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| #17545 | +1206/-24, 17 files, `packages/cloud/shared` | FAILED | FAILED |\n| #17546 | +356/-39, 2 files, Discord onboarding | FAILED | passed |\n\n**Develop PR Gate** — [run 30701753824](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30701753824),\n81 polls over ~40 minutes:\n\n```\npoll 81: passed=0 waiting=0 failed=7\nFAILED lint:               no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml\nFAILED typecheck:          no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml\nFAILED build:              no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/develop-pr.yml\nFAILED gitleaks:           no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml\nFAILED check-pr-evidence:  no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/pr.yaml\nFAILED check-pr-title:     no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/pr.yaml\nFAILED stale-base guard:   no GitHub Actions check run from .github/workflows/stale-base-guard.yml\n```\n\n**Security Advisory Gate** — [run 30701716047](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30701716047),\n~40 polls over 20 minutes:\n\n```\nwaiting for deterministic security checks: gitleaks\n...\nscripts/security/security-advisory-gate.mjs:148\nError: timed out waiting for security advisory checks\n```\n\nWorkflow run states on the same branch at that moment — none had started:\n\n```\ngitleaks         | completed | action_required | pull_request\nCloud Tests      | completed | action_required | pull_request\nDevelop PR       | completed | action_required | pull_request\nSecurity Review  | completed | action_required | pull_request\nQuality (Fork)   | completed | action_required | pull_request\n… 13 workflows total\n```\n\nThe Security Advisory Gate difference between the two PRs is scope, not health:\nit did not require `gitleaks` for the smaller diff.\n\n## Why the existing approval handling does not cover this\n\n`security-advisory-gate.mjs` already models approval latency — `approvalDeadline`\nplus `requiredChecksStartedBy()` grants a bounded completion grace when required\nchecks *started* before the deadline. That handles \"approved, but slow\".\n\nIt does not distinguish that from \"held at `action_required`, so it will never\nstart\". In the second case the wait cannot succeed by construction, but the gate\nstill consumes its whole budget before reporting a failure whose message\n(\"timed out\") does not name the actual cause.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nTreat a required check whose workflow run is `action_required` as *not yet\napproved* rather than *pending*:\n\n- fail fast with an explicit message (\"required workflows awaiting maintainer\n  approval: …\") instead of polling to exhaustion, or\n- skip the gate for fork PRs until approval lands, letting it run on the\n  post-approval re-run.\n\nEither turns a silent 20-40 minute timeout into an immediate, actionable\nstatement, and stops burning runner capacity on a wait that cannot resolve. It\nalso stops a reviewer seeing seven red required checks that never ran.\n\nBoth gates share the shape, so whichever fix applies probably wants to apply to\nboth.\n\n## Notes\n\n- This is reported from the outside, based on two runs; if the current behaviour\n  is deliberate — a gate cannot know a check will never arrive — feel free to\n  close.\n- I have not claimed this.
